title: Prices Are Rising Faster Than Expected
summary:
Prices in the United States are going up faster than experts expected. That is what a new report about inflation showed on Wednesday. Inflation means the cost of everyday things goes up, so the same money buys less.

The report found that prices were 3.7 percent higher than a year ago.

Heather Long is an economist, a person who studies money and the economy. She told PBS NewsHour that about half of the rise came from high gas and diesel prices. The other half came from many other things, like medical care, toys, clothes and car repairs.

Long said the Federal Reserve will likely need to raise interest rates again. She also said wages are growing by only about 3 percent, so many paychecks are not keeping up with prices.

Some families said they must watch their money closely. The report comes three weeks before the midterm elections.
why_it_matters: When prices go up faster than paychecks, families may have less money for things like food, clothes and fun.

keywords.explanation: Inflation is when prices go up over time, so money buys less.
An economist is a person who studies money and how the economy works.
Diesel is a kind of fuel used by trucks, tractors and some cars.
Interest rates are the extra money people pay when they borrow money.
Wages are the money people get paid for working.
Midterm elections are U.S. elections held halfway between presidential elections.
